source

CalendarHeatmap

def CalendarHeatmap(
    data, start, end, level_max:int=4, thresholds:NoneType=None, palette:NoneType=None, as_of:NoneType=None,
    show_months:bool=True, show_weekdays:bool=True, show_legend:bool=True
):

Rich renderable: GitHub-style annual activity heatmap from {date: value}.

source


default_palette

def default_palette(
    level_max
):

Built-in GitHub-green palette of length level_max+1 (level 0 = empty).

from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail

# default palette length = level_max + 1
test_eq(len(default_palette(4)), 5)
test_eq(len(default_palette(3)), 4)
test_fail(lambda: default_palette(9), contains="palette")

# valid construction resolves thresholds and per-year blocks
hm = CalendarHeatmap({date(2026, 1, 1): 3, date(2026, 1, 2): 9},
                     date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31))
test_eq(len(hm.thresholds), 3)            # level_max-1
test_eq(len(hm.palette), 5)
test_eq([y for y, _, _ in hm.blocks], [2026])

# validation
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 2, 1), date(2026, 1, 1)), contains="start")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), level_max=0), contains="level_max")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), thresholds=[1, 2]), contains="length")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), thresholds=[3, 2, 1]), contains="non-decreasing")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({date(2026, 1, 2): -1}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)), contains="finite")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), palette=["a", "b"]), contains="palette")

# data must be a Mapping with datetime.date keys; thresholds must be finite
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap([(date(2026, 1, 1), 5)], date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)), contains="Mapping")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({"2026-01-01": 5}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)), contains="date")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({datetime(2026, 1, 1): 5}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31)), contains="date")
test_fail(lambda: CalendarHeatmap({date(2026, 1, 1): 5}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), thresholds=[float("nan"), 2, 3]), contains="finite")

# a bad value on a FUTURE day must NOT raise (validation is observed-only)
CalendarHeatmap({date(2026, 12, 30): -1}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), as_of=date(2026, 6, 23))

<__main__.CalendarHeatmap at 0x7fbf9abaa840>



source


rich_console

def __rich_console__(
    console, options
):

Call self as a function.

from fastcore.test import test_eq
from rich.console import Console

def _render(hm, width=240):
    c = Console(record=True, width=width, force_terminal=False)
    c.print(hm)
    return c.export_text()

data = {date(2026, 1, 1) + timedelta(days=i): (i % 5) for i in range(120)}
out = _render(CalendarHeatmap(data, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 4, 30)))
assert "Su" in out and "Sa" in out          # weekday labels
assert "Jan" in out and "Feb" in out        # month labels
assert "Less" in out and "More" in out      # legend
assert "■" in out                           # filled cells

# multi-year stacks show year labels
out_my = _render(CalendarHeatmap(data, date(2025, 12, 1), date(2026, 4, 30)))
assert "2025" in out_my and "2026" in out_my

# future region uses the placeholder glyph
out_fut = _render(CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 12, 31), as_of=date(2026, 6, 23)))
assert "·" in out_fut

# as_of < start => the whole grid is future: no filled square before the legend
out_all = _render(CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 6, 1), date(2026, 6, 30), as_of=date(2026, 1, 1)))
grid_part = out_all.split("Less")[0]
assert "·" in grid_part and "■" not in grid_part

# toggles drop their chrome
out_bare = _render(CalendarHeatmap(data, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 4, 30),
                                   show_months=False, show_weekdays=False, show_legend=False))
assert "Jan" not in out_bare and "Less" not in out_bare and "Su" not in out_bare

# in-window cell count == inclusive day count; padding is blank, no future cells
out_cc = _render(CalendarHeatmap({}, date(2026, 3, 2), date(2026, 3, 15)))
grid_cc = out_cc.split("Less")[0]
assert grid_cc.count("■") == 14      # 2026-03-02..2026-03-15 inclusive, all level-0 observed
assert "·" not in grid_cc            # as_of is None -> no future cells

title: levels
text:
source

quantile_thresholds

def quantile_thresholds(
    values, level_max
):

Ascending cut points (len level_max-1) splitting positive values into level_max groups.

source


to_level

def to_level(
    value, thresholds
):

Integer activity level 0..len(thresholds)+1; 0 when value<=0.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

# to_level: 0/negative -> level 0; positives bucket by bisect_right
test_eq(to_level(0, [1, 5, 10]), 0)
test_eq(to_level(-3, [1, 5, 10]), 0)
test_eq(to_level(0.5, [1, 5, 10]), 1)
test_eq(to_level(1, [1, 5, 10]), 2)
test_eq(to_level(7, [1, 5, 10]), 3)
test_eq(to_level(999, [1, 5, 10]), 4)

# quantile_thresholds: length is level_max - 1, positives only, ties allowed
test_eq(len(quantile_thresholds([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8], 4)), 3)
test_eq(quantile_thresholds([5], 4), [])              # <2 positive -> []
test_eq(quantile_thresholds([1, 2, 3], 1), [])        # level_max==1 -> []
test_eq(quantile_thresholds([0, 0, 5, 5], 4), [5.0, 5.0, 5.0])  # non-positive ignored; ties ok

weekday_row

def weekday_row(
    d
):

Row index with Sunday=0 .. Saturday=6.

from fastcore.test import test_eq

# 2024-01-07 is a Sunday, 2024-01-06 a Saturday, 2023-12-31 a Sunday
test_eq(weekday_row(date(2024, 1, 7)), 0)
test_eq(weekday_row(date(2024, 1, 6)), 6)
test_eq(sunday_on_or_before(date(2024, 1, 1)), date(2023, 12, 31))
test_eq(sunday_on_or_before(date(2024, 1, 7)), date(2024, 1, 7))
test_eq(saturday_on_or_after(date(2024, 1, 1)), date(2024, 1, 6))
test_eq(saturday_on_or_after(date(2024, 1, 6)), date(2024, 1, 6))
test_eq(week_col(date(2024, 1, 7), date(2023, 12, 31)), 1)
test_eq(grid_bounds(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 1, 13)), (date(2023, 12, 31), 2))

month_label_cols

def month_label_cols(
    block_start, block_end, grid_start
):

List of (week_col, ‘Mon’) for the first day of each month in [block_start, block_end].

source


year_blocks

def year_blocks(
    start, end
):

Split [start, end] into (year, block_start, block_end); one block per calendar year.

from fastcore.test import test_eq, test_fail

# single calendar year -> one block
test_eq(year_blocks(date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 6, 23)),
        [(2026, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 6, 23))])

# multi-year -> one block per year, clipped
b = year_blocks(date(2024, 11, 1), date(2026, 2, 1))
test_eq([y for y, _, _ in b], [2024, 2025, 2026])
test_eq(b[0], (2024, date(2024, 11, 1), date(2024, 12, 31)))
test_eq(b[1], (2025, date(2025, 1, 1), date(2025, 12, 31)))
test_eq(b[2], (2026, date(2026, 1, 1), date(2026, 2, 1)))

test_fail(lambda: year_blocks(date(2026, 2, 1), date(2026, 1, 1)), contains="start")

# month labels in order
gs = sunday_on_or_before(date(2024, 1, 1))
test_eq([l for _, l in month_label_cols(date(2024, 1, 1), date(2024, 3, 31), gs)],
        ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar"])

Developer Guide
If you are new to using nbdev here are some useful pointers to get you started.

Install richcal in Development mode
# make sure richcal package is installed in development mode
$ pip install -e .

# make changes under nbs/ directory
# ...

# compile to have changes apply to richcal
$ nbdev_prepare

title: richcal
text:
Usage

Installation
Install latest from the GitHub repository:
$ pip install git+https://github.com/doyu/richcal.git
or from conda
$ conda install -c doyu richcal
or from pypi
$ pip install richcal


Documentation
Documentation can be found hosted on this GitHub repository’s pages. Additionally you can find package manager specific guidelines on conda and pypi respectively.
